paragraphs.text: When therefore the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John
paragraphs.original: Ὡς οὖν ἔγνω ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἤκουσαν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ὅτι Ἰησοῦς πλείονας μαθητὰς ποιεῖ καὶ βαπτίζει ἢ Ἰωάννης—
paragraphs.translit: Hōs oun egnō ho Iēsous hoti ēkousan hoi Pharisaioi hoti Iēsous pleionas mathētas poiei kai baptizei ē Iōannēs—

paragraphs.text: (although Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples),
paragraphs.original: καίτοιγε Ἰησοῦς αὐτὸς οὐκ ἐβάπτιζεν ἀλλʼ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ—
paragraphs.translit: kaitoige Iēsous autos ouk ebaptizen allʼ hoi mathētai autou—

paragraphs.text: he left Judea, and departed again into Galilee.
paragraphs.original: ἀφῆκεν τὴν Ἰουδαίαν καὶ ἀπῆλθεν πάλιν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
paragraphs.translit: aphēken tēn Ioudaian kai apēlthen palin eis tēn Galilaian.

paragraphs.text: And he must needs pass through Samaria.
paragraphs.original: ἔδει δὲ αὐτὸν διέρχεσθαι διὰ τῆς Σαμαρείας.
paragraphs.translit: edei de auton dierchesthai dia tēs Samareias.

paragraphs.text: So he cometh to a city of Samaria, called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph:
paragraphs.original: ἔρχεται οὖν εἰς πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας λεγομένην Συχὰρ πλησίον τοῦ χωρίου ὃ ἔδωκεν Ἰακὼβ τῷ Ἰωσὴφ τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: erchetai oun eis polin tēs Samareias legomenēn Sychar plēsion tou chōriou ho edōken Iakōb tō Iōsēph tō hyiō autou·

paragraphs.text: and Jacob`s well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus by the well. It was about the sixth hour.
paragraphs.original: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πηγὴ τοῦ Ἰακώβ. ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς κεκοπιακὼς ἐκ τῆς ὁδοιπορίας ἐκαθέζετο οὕτως ἐπὶ τῇ πηγῇ· ὥρα ἦν ὡς ἕκτη.
paragraphs.translit: ēn de ekei pēgē tou Iakōb. ho oun Iēsous kekopiakōs ek tēs hodoiporias ekathezeto houtōs epi tē pēgē· hōra ēn hōs hektē.

paragraphs.text: There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink.
paragraphs.original: Ἔρχεται γυνὴ ἐκ τῆς Σαμαρείας ἀντλῆσαι ὕδωρ. λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Δός μοι πεῖν·
paragraphs.translit: Erchetai gynē ek tēs Samareias antlēsai hydōr. legei autē ho Iēsous· Dos moi pein·

paragraphs.text: For his disciples were gone away into the city to buy food.
paragraphs.original: οἱ γὰρ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἀπεληλύθεισαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, ἵνα τροφὰς ἀγοράσωσιν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi gar mathētai autou apelēlytheisan eis tēn polin, hina trophas agorasōsin.

paragraphs.text: The Samaritan woman therefore saith unto him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, who am a Samaritan woman? (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)
paragraphs.original: λέγει οὖν αὐτῷ ἡ γυνὴ ἡ Σαμαρῖτις· Πῶς σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ὢν παρʼ ἐμοῦ πεῖν αἰτεῖς γυναικὸς Σαμαρίτιδος οὔσης; οὐ γὰρ συγχρῶνται Ἰουδαῖοι Σαμαρίταις.
paragraphs.translit: legei oun autō hē gynē hē Samaritis· Pōs sy Ioudaios ōn parʼ emou pein aiteis gynaikos Samaritidos ousēs; ou gar synchrōntai Ioudaioi Samaritais.

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered and said unto unto her, If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Εἰ ᾔδεις τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ λέγων σοι· Δός μοι πεῖν, σὺ ἂν ᾔτησας αὐτὸν καὶ ἔδωκεν ἄν σοι ὕδωρ ζῶν.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē Iēsous kai eipen autē· Ei ēdeis tēn dōrean tou theou kai tis estin ho legōn soi· Dos moi pein, sy an ētēsas auton kai edōken an soi hydōr zōn.

paragraphs.text: The woman saith unto him, Sir, thou hast nothing to draw with, and the well is deep: whence then hast thou that living water?
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ γυνή· Κύριε, οὔτε ἄντλημα ἔχεις καὶ τὸ φρέαρ ἐστὶν βαθύ· πόθεν οὖν ἔχεις τὸ ὕδωρ τὸ ζῶν;
paragraphs.translit: legei autō hē gynē· Kyrie, oute antlēma echeis kai to phrear estin bathy· pothen oun echeis to hydōr to zōn;

paragraphs.text: Art thou greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his sons, and his cattle?
paragraphs.original: μὴ σὺ μείζων εἶ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἰακώβ, ὃς ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν τὸ φρέαρ καὶ αὐτὸς ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔπιεν καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ θρέμματα αὐτοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: mē sy meizōn ei tou patros hēmōn Iakōb, hos edōken hēmin to phrear kai autos ex autou epien kai hoi hyioi autou kai ta thremmata autou;

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered and said unto her, Every one that drinketh of this water shall thirst again:
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Πᾶς ὁ πίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος τούτου διψήσει πάλιν·
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē Iēsous kai eipen autē· Pas ho pinōn ek tou hydatos toutou dipsēsei palin·

paragraphs.text: but whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall become in him a well of water springing up unto eternal life.
paragraphs.original: ὃς δʼ ἂν πίῃ ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος οὗ ἐγὼ δώσω αὐτῷ, οὐ μὴ διψήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἀλλὰ τὸ ὕδωρ ὃ δώσω αὐτῷ γενήσεται ἐν αὐτῷ πηγὴ ὕδατος ἁλλομένου εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
paragraphs.translit: hos dʼ an piē ek tou hydatos hou egō dōsō autō, ou mē dipsēsei eis ton aiōna, alla to hydōr ho dōsō autō genēsetai en autō pēgē hydatos hallomenou eis zōēn aiōnion.

paragraphs.text: The woman saith unto him, Sir, give me this water, that I thirst not, neither come all the way hither to draw.
paragraphs.original: λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ γυνή· Κύριε, δός μοι τοῦτο τὸ ὕδωρ, ἵνα μὴ διψῶ μηδὲ διέρχωμαι ἐνθάδε ἀντλεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: legei pros auton hē gynē· Kyrie, dos moi touto to hydōr, hina mē dipsō mēde dierchōmai enthade antlein.

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith unto her, Go, call thy husband, and come hither.
paragraphs.original: Λέγει αὐτῇ· Ὕπαγε φώνησον τὸν ἄνδρα σου καὶ ἐλθὲ ἐνθάδε.
paragraphs.translit: Legei autē· Hypage phōnēson ton andra sou kai elthe enthade.

paragraphs.text: The woman answered and said unto him, I have no husband. Jesus saith unto her, Thou saidst well, I have no husband:
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη ἡ γυνὴ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Οὐκ ἔχω ἄνδρα. λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Καλῶς εἶπας ὅτι Ἄνδρα οὐκ ἔχω·
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē hē gynē kai eipen autō· Ouk echō andra. legei autē ho Iēsous· Kalōs eipas hoti Andra ouk echō·

paragraphs.text: for thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: this hast thou said truly.
paragraphs.original: πέντε γὰρ ἄνδρας ἔσχες, καὶ νῦν ὃν ἔχεις οὐκ ἔστιν σου ἀνήρ· τοῦτο ἀληθὲς εἴρηκας.
paragraphs.translit: pente gar andras esches, kai nyn hon echeis ouk estin sou anēr· touto alēthes eirēkas.

paragraphs.text: The woman saith unto him, Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ γυνή· Κύριε, θεωρῶ ὅτι προφήτης εἶ σύ.
paragraphs.translit: legei autō hē gynē· Kyrie, theōrō hoti prophētēs ei sy.

paragraphs.text: Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.
paragraphs.original: οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ προσεκύνησαν· καὶ ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐστὶν ὁ τόπος ὅπου προσκυνεῖν δεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: hoi pateres hēmōn en tō orei toutō prosekynēsan· kai hymeis legete hoti en Hierosolymois estin ho topos hopou proskynein dei.

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when neither in this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, shall ye worship the Father.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πίστευέ μοι, γύναι, ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα ὅτε οὔτε ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ οὔτε ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις προσκυνήσετε τῷ πατρί.
paragraphs.translit: legei autē ho Iēsous· Pisteue moi, gynai, hoti erchetai hōra hote oute en tō orei toutō oute en Hierosolymois proskynēsete tō patri.

paragraphs.text: Ye worship that which ye know not: we worship that which we know; for salvation is from the Jews.
paragraphs.original: ὑμεῖς προσκυνεῖτε ὃ οὐκ οἴδατε, ἡμεῖς προσκυνοῦμεν ὃ οἴδαμεν, ὅτι ἡ σωτηρία ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐστίν·
paragraphs.translit: hymeis proskyneite ho ouk oidate, hēmeis proskynoumen ho oidamen, hoti hē sōtēria ek tōn Ioudaiōn estin·

paragraphs.text: But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and truth: for such doth the Father seek to be his worshippers.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ νῦν ἐστιν, ὅτε οἱ ἀληθινοὶ προσκυνηταὶ προσκυνήσουσιν τῷ πατρὶ ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἀληθείᾳ, καὶ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ τοιούτους ζητεῖ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: alla erchetai hōra kai nyn estin, hote hoi alēthinoi proskynētai proskynēsousin tō patri en pneumati kai alētheia, kai gar ho patēr toioutous zētei tous proskynountas auton·

paragraphs.text: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship in spirit and truth.
paragraphs.original: πνεῦμα ὁ θεός, καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας αὐτὸν ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἀληθείᾳ δεῖ προσκυνεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: pneuma ho theos, kai tous proskynountas auton en pneumati kai alētheia dei proskynein.

paragraphs.text: The woman saith unto him, I know that Messiah cometh (he that is called Christ): when he is come, he will declare unto us all things.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ γυνή· Οἶδα ὅτι Μεσσίας ἔρχεται, ὁ λεγόμενος χριστός· ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐκεῖνος, ἀναγγελεῖ ἡμῖν ἅπαντα.
paragraphs.translit: legei autō hē gynē· Oida hoti Messias erchetai, ho legomenos christos· hotan elthē ekeinos, anangelei hēmin hapanta.

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am [he].
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐγώ εἰμι, ὁ λαλῶν σοι.
paragraphs.translit: legei autē ho Iēsous· Egō eimi, ho lalōn soi.

paragraphs.text: And upon this came his disciples; and they marvelled that he was speaking with a woman; yet no man said, What seekest thou? or, Why speakest thou with her?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἦλθαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ὅτι μετὰ γυναικὸς ἐλάλει· οὐδεὶς μέντοι εἶπεν· Τί ζητεῖς; ἢ τί λαλεῖς μετʼ αὐτῆς;
paragraphs.translit: Kai epi toutō ēlthan hoi mathētai autou, kai ethaumazon hoti meta gynaikos elalei· oudeis mentoi eipen· Ti zēteis; ē ti laleis metʼ autēs;

paragraphs.text: So the woman left her waterpot, and went away into the city, and saith to the people,
paragraphs.original: ἀφῆκεν οὖν τὴν ὑδρίαν αὐτῆς ἡ γυνὴ καὶ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ λέγει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις·
paragraphs.translit: aphēken oun tēn hydrian autēs hē gynē kai apēlthen eis tēn polin kai legei tois anthrōpois·

paragraphs.text: Come, see a man, who told me all things that [ever] I did: can this be the Christ?
paragraphs.original: Δεῦτε ἴδετε ἄνθρωπον ὃς εἶπέ μοι πάντα ὅσα ἐποίησα· μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός;
paragraphs.translit: Deute idete anthrōpon hos eipe moi panta hosa epoiēsa· mēti houtos estin ho christos;

paragraphs.text: They went out of the city, and were coming to him.
paragraphs.original: ἐξῆλθον ἐκ τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: exēlthon ek tēs poleōs kai ērchonto pros auton.

paragraphs.text: In the mean while the disciples prayed him, saying, Rabbi, eat.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ ἠρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες· Ῥαββί, φάγε.
paragraphs.translit: En tō metaxy ērōtōn auton hoi mathētai legontes· Rhabbi, phage.

paragraphs.text: But he said unto them, I have meat to eat that ye know not.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐγὼ βρῶσιν ἔχω φαγεῖν ἣν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autois· Egō brōsin echō phagein hēn hymeis ouk oidate.

paragraphs.text: The disciples therefore said one to another, Hath any man brought him [aught] to eat?
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Μή τις ἤνεγκεν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν;
paragraphs.translit: elegon oun hoi mathētai pros allēlous· Mē tis ēnenken autō phagein;

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith unto them, My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to accomplish his work.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐμὸν βρῶμά ἐστιν ἵνα ποιήσω τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με καὶ τελειώσω αὐτοῦ τὸ ἔργον.
paragraphs.translit: legei autois ho Iēsous· Emon brōma estin hina poiēsō to thelēma tou pempsantos me kai teleiōsō autou to ergon.

paragraphs.text: Say not ye, There are yet four months, and [then] cometh the harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields, that they are white already unto harvest.
paragraphs.original: οὐχ ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι Ἔτι τετράμηνός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ θερισμὸς ἔρχεται; ἰδοὺ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐπάρατε τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὑμῶν καὶ θεάσασθε τὰς χώρας ὅτι λευκαί εἰσιν πρὸς θερισμόν· ἤδη
paragraphs.translit: ouch hymeis legete hoti Eti tetramēnos estin kai ho therismos erchetai; idou legō hymin, eparate tous ophthalmous hymōn kai theasasthe tas chōras hoti leukai eisin pros therismon· ēdē

paragraphs.text: He that reapeth receiveth wages, and gathereth fruit unto life eternal; that he that soweth and he that reapeth may rejoice together.
paragraphs.original: ὁ θερίζων μισθὸν λαμβάνει καὶ συνάγει καρπὸν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, ἵνα ὁ σπείρων ὁμοῦ χαίρῃ καὶ ὁ θερίζων.
paragraphs.translit: ho therizōn misthon lambanei kai synagei karpon eis zōēn aiōnion, hina ho speirōn homou chairē kai ho therizōn.

paragraphs.text: For herein is the saying true, One soweth, and another reapeth.
paragraphs.original: ἐν γὰρ τούτῳ ὁ λόγος ἐστὶν ἀληθινὸς ὅτι Ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ σπείρων καὶ ἄλλος ὁ θερίζων·
paragraphs.translit: en gar toutō ho logos estin alēthinos hoti Allos estin ho speirōn kai allos ho therizōn·

paragraphs.text: I sent you to reap that whereon ye have not labored: others have labored, and ye are entered into their labor.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς θερίζειν ὃ οὐχ ὑμεῖς κεκοπιάκατε· ἄλλοι κεκοπιάκασιν, καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν κόπον αὐτῶν εἰσεληλύθατε.
paragraphs.translit: egō apesteila hymas therizein ho ouch hymeis kekopiakate· alloi kekopiakasin, kai hymeis eis ton kopon autōn eiselēlythate.

paragraphs.text: And from that city many of the Samaritans believed on him because of the word of the woman, who testified, He told me all things that [ever] I did.
paragraphs.original: Ἐκ δὲ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν τῶν Σαμαριτῶν διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς γυναικὸς μαρτυρούσης ὅτι Εἶπέν μοι πάντα ἃ ἐποίησα.
paragraphs.translit: Ek de tēs poleōs ekeinēs polloi episteusan eis auton tōn Samaritōn dia ton logon tēs gynaikos martyrousēs hoti Eipen moi panta ha epoiēsa.

paragraphs.text: So when the Samaritans came unto him, they besought him to abide with them: and he abode there two days.
paragraphs.original: ὡς οὖν ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Σαμαρῖται, ἠρώτων αὐτὸν μεῖναι παρʼ αὐτοῖς· καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐκεῖ δύο ἡμέρας.
paragraphs.translit: hōs oun ēlthon pros auton hoi Samaritai, ērōtōn auton meinai parʼ autois· kai emeinen ekei dyo hēmeras.

paragraphs.text: And many more believed because of his word;
paragraphs.original: καὶ πολλῷ πλείους ἐπίστευσαν διὰ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: kai pollō pleious episteusan dia ton logon autou,

paragraphs.text: and they said to the woman, Now we believe, not because of thy speaking: for we have heard for ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Saviour of the world.
paragraphs.original: τῇ τε γυναικὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὐκέτι διὰ τὴν σὴν λαλιὰν πιστεύομεν· αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀκηκόαμεν, καὶ οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ σωτὴρ τοῦ κόσμου.
paragraphs.translit: tē te gynaiki elegon hoti Ouketi dia tēn sēn lalian pisteuomen· autoi gar akēkoamen, kai oidamen hoti houtos estin alēthōs ho sōtēr tou kosmou.

paragraphs.text: And after the two days he went forth from thence into Galilee.
paragraphs.original: Μετὰ δὲ τὰς δύο ἡμέρας ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν·
paragraphs.translit: Meta de tas dyo hēmeras exēlthen ekeithen eis tēn Galilaian·

paragraphs.text: For Jesus himself testified, that a prophet hath no honor in his own country.
paragraphs.original: αὐτὸς γὰρ Ἰησοῦς ἐμαρτύρησεν ὅτι προφήτης ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ πατρίδι τιμὴν οὐκ ἔχει.
paragraphs.translit: autos gar Iēsous emartyrēsen hoti prophētēs en tē idia patridi timēn ouk echei.

paragraphs.text: So when he came into Galilee, the Galilaeans received him, having seen all the things that he did in Jerusalem at the feast: for they also went unto the feast.
paragraphs.original: ὅτε οὖν ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, ἐδέξαντο αὐτὸν οἱ Γαλιλαῖοι, πάντα ἑωρακότες ὅσα ἐποίησεν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, καὶ αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἦλθον εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν.
paragraphs.translit: hote oun ēlthen eis tēn Galilaian, edexanto auton hoi Galilaioi, panta heōrakotes hosa epoiēsen en Hierosolymois en tē heortē, kai autoi gar ēlthon eis tēn heortēn.

paragraphs.text: He came therefore again unto Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain nobleman, whose son was sick at Capernaum.
paragraphs.original: Ἦλθεν οὖν πάλιν εἰς τὴν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, ὅπου ἐποίησεν τὸ ὕδωρ οἶνον. καὶ ἦν τις βασιλικὸς οὗ ὁ υἱὸς ἠσθένει ἐν Καφαρναούμ.
paragraphs.translit: Ēlthen oun palin eis tēn Kana tēs Galilaias, hopou epoiēsen to hydōr oinon. kai ēn tis basilikos hou ho hyios ēsthenei en Kapharnaoum.

paragraphs.text: When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judaea into Galilee, he went unto him, and besought [him] that he would come down, and heal his son; for he was at the point of death.
paragraphs.original: οὗτος ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἥκει ἐκ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ἠρώτα ἵνα καταβῇ καὶ ἰάσηται αὐτοῦ τὸν υἱόν, ἤμελλεν γὰρ ἀποθνῄσκειν.
paragraphs.translit: houtos akousas hoti Iēsous hēkei ek tēs Ioudaias eis tēn Galilaian apēlthen pros auton kai ērōta hina katabē kai iasētai autou ton hyion, ēmellen gar apothnēskein.

paragraphs.text: Jesus therefore said unto him, Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will in no wise believe.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἐὰν μὴ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἴδητε, οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε.
paragraphs.translit: eipen oun ho Iēsous pros auton· Ean mē sēmeia kai terata idēte, ou mē pisteusēte.

paragraphs.text: The nobleman saith unto him, Sir, come down ere my child die.
paragraphs.original: λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ βασιλικός· Κύριε, κατάβηθι πρὶν ἀποθανεῖν τὸ παιδίον μου.
paragraphs.translit: legei pros auton ho basilikos· Kyrie, katabēthi prin apothanein to paidion mou.

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith unto him, Go thy way; thy son liveth. The man believed the word that Jesus spake unto him, and he went his way.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πορεύου· ὁ υἱός σου ζῇ. ἐπίστευσεν ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ λόγῳ ὃν εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἐπορεύετο.
paragraphs.translit: legei autō ho Iēsous· Poreuou· ho hyios sou zē. episteusen ho anthrōpos tō logō hon eipen autō ho Iēsous kai eporeueto.

paragraphs.text: And as he was now going down, his servants met him, saying, that his son lived.
paragraphs.original: ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ καταβαίνοντος οἱ δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ ὑπήντησαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες ὅτι ὁ παῖς αὐτοῦ ζῇ.
paragraphs.translit: ēdē de autou katabainontos hoi douloi autou hypēntēsan autō legontes hoti ho pais autou zē.

paragraphs.text: So he inquired of them the hour when he began to amend. They said therefore unto him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.
paragraphs.original: ἐπύθετο οὖν τὴν ὥραν παρʼ αὐτῶν ἐν ᾗ κομψότερον ἔσχεν· εἶπαν οὖν αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἐχθὲς ὥραν ἑβδόμην ἀφῆκεν αὐτὸν ὁ πυρετός.
paragraphs.translit: epytheto oun tēn hōran parʼ autōn en hē kompsoteron eschen· eipan oun autō hoti Echthes hōran hebdomēn aphēken auton ho pyretos.

paragraphs.text: So the father knew that [it was] at that hour in which Jesus said unto him, Thy son liveth: and himself believed, and his whole house.
paragraphs.original: ἔγνω οὖν ὁ πατὴρ ὅτι ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐν ᾗ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὁ υἱός σου ζῇ, καὶ ἐπίστευσεν αὐτὸς καὶ ἡ οἰκία αὐτοῦ ὅλη.
paragraphs.translit: egnō oun ho patēr hoti ekeinē tē hōra en hē eipen autō ho Iēsous· Ho hyios sou zē, kai episteusen autos kai hē oikia autou holē.

paragraphs.text: This is again the second sign that Jesus did, having come out of Judaea into Galilee.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δὲ πάλιν δεύτερον σημεῖον ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλθὼν ἐκ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
paragraphs.translit: touto de palin deuteron sēmeion epoiēsen ho Iēsous elthōn ek tēs Ioudaias eis tēn Galilaian.
